results.title: Cape Verde could make election history with first female president
results.content: Cape Verde goes to the polls on Sunday in an election that could see the African island nation appoint its first ever female leader. Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent José Maria Neves, who is the country's fifth president since it became independent from Portugal in 1975.

results.title: 'Is this a cyberattack?' Grounded flights, a Microsoft outage and AI chaos fuel cybersecurity fears
results.content: A series of unsettling disruptions, from tech stock turbulence and Microsoft outages to a nationwide grounding of flights, has left millions wondering whether the world’s increasingly interconnected technology systems are beginning to unravel.

results.title: SpaceX's Starship completes first-ever mid-air catch after return from orbit
results.content: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft made a successful return to Earth on Saturday, completing its first mid-air catch by giant robot arms in Texas, after an aborted recovery attempt.

results.title: Netanyahu renews call for Israeli unity government as Eisenkot dismisses 'tricks'
results.content: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday renewed his call for a national unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, who dismissed the appeal as a political ploy. This comes as the incoming premier is in the midst of negotiations to form a new administration.

results.title: Macron says limiting Ukraine aid would pave way to 'another war'
results.content: French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday warned that limiting aid to Ukraine would force Kyiv into an "unjust peace" and risk another war. His statement comes as the United States pushes ahead with efforts to negotiate between Ukraine and Moscow.

results.title: 'No justice, no peace': Fifth round of protests sweep across France
results.content: Between 106,000 and 200,000 people took to the streets across France on Saturday for the fifth round of protests, according to figures from the interior ministry and student unions respectively, as turnout fell and some incidents were reported.

results.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX aborts booster recovery due to technical issues
results.content: Elon Musk's SpaceX is in the midst of a 15th test-flight of its Starship rocket. The company was hoping to pull off the first-ever "double catch" - with both the booster and the ship itself coming safely back down to earth. Instead, an unspecified problem forced the company to abort recovery of the booster, which was diverted from its return path and crashed down into the Gulf of Mexico. Analysis by journalist Frédéric Castel, based in Bosa Chica, Texas, USA.

results.title: Youth Olympic Games organisers hail Senegal's capability to host major events
results.content: Dakar 2026 is over. Two weeks of competition, thousands of young athletes and a historic first for Africa. The Youth Olympic Games brought the world to Senegal for the first Olympic sporting event ever held on the continent. From record-breaking performances to historic medals for the host nation, Dakar 2026 has been a celebration of sport, youth and cultural exchange. Our correspondent Aminatou Diallo reports from Dakar.

results.title: France and Cambodia share their love for pétanque in Phnom Penh
results.content: Phnom Penh is hosting the 20th Francophonie Summit this Sunday and Monday. French President Emmanuel Macron is attending as part of a 3-day state visit to Cambodia. France and Cambodia's history is deep rooted and complex, but the two countries have one thing in common: a love for pétanque. Story by Caitlin Brown.

results.title: Washington divided over how to deal with fallout from the Nvidia case
results.content: After the fall, the fallout. US government agencies are squabbling after AI leader Jensen Huang stepped down from chips giant Nvidia in disgrace. The Treasury says it wanted to blacklist a Singapore company at the heart of the scandal, but the Commerce Department didn't act. Megaspeed was run by suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who reportedly had an affair with Jensen Huang. Details by Peter O'Brien.

results.title: US: What exactly caused the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years?
results.content: After a nearly five-hour ground stoppage, flights in the US have resumed. However, officials are warning that it will take days to recover from the ongoing delays related to the incident. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy explained the crisis was due to a failure in ageing telecommunications equipment. What exactly happened? Answers with FRANCE 24 international affairs editor Shirli Sitbon.

results.title: US Transport Secretary asks Congress for $30 bn to upgrade aviation infrastructure
results.content: A failure in aging telecommunications equipment Friday forced a nationwide halt to departures from US airports. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin says officials have found no evidence so far of a cyberattack, but that they're not ruling it out. Details by Jack Pownall.

results.title: Wales claim historic victory against All Blacks for first time since 1953
results.content: Wales claimed a historic 35-28 victory over New Zealand in Cardiff on Saturday, securing their first win over the All Blacks since 1953.

results.title: Copper wires to blame for US flight disruption, says Trump administration
results.content: With thousands of flights cancelled and travel disruption continuing, officials say the situation should return to normal Sunday. The Trump administration pointed to aging infrastructure – specifically "a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines" – as being responsible for nationwide travel chaos.

results.title: 'Poisoned chalice': French presidential hopeful Riner rebuffs Macron's backing
results.content: French judo champion Teddy Riner on Saturday publicly distanced himself from President Emmanuel Macron, calling his endorsement a "poisoned chalice". The presidential hopeful seeks to position himself as an alternative to France's political extremes.

results.title: DR Congo, Rwanda clash over Francophonie leadership as Macron seeks compromise
results.content: DR Congo and Rwanda clashed Saturday over the leadership of the Francophonie, as tensions between the neighbouring countries spilled into the race to head the 53-member organisation. French President Emmanuel Macron urged Rwanda to withdraw its candidate in favour of a compromise choice ahead of Monday's vote.

results.title: 'I never imagined my father was a Nazi': Born in a German-run 'baby factory'
results.content: Two trainloads of children, some of them born in Nazi-run "Lebensborn" maternity homes, were brought from Germany to Commercy in eastern France in 1946. One of those on board was Édith Pagot.

results.title: USA: All passengers survive after tanker hits docked river cruise ship in New Orleans
results.content: A portion of the Mississippi River remains closed after a collision between an oil tanker and a riverboat forced a chaotic river rescue in Louisiana. Story by Caitlin Brown.

results.title: Inside Ethiopia's war: Rare access to a hospital treating victims of renewed fighting
results.content: Ethiopia's renewed conflict is taking an increasing toll on civilians, with humanitarian organisations reporting a rise in casualties. In the Amhara region, FRANCE 24’s correspondent Tom Canetti was granted rare access to a civilian hospital where surgeons are struggling to treat the influx of wounded patients. But for many caught in the fighting, reaching medical care is a challenge in itself. Warning: The report contains images of surgery that may be confronting for some viewers.

results.title: Who are the 'street medics' showing up at protests around the world?
results.content: From treating tear gas exposure to tending to injuries, street medics have become an increasingly common sight at protests all over the world. But who exactly are they and when did they start showing up at demonstrations? Story by Daniel Quinlan.

results.title: U2 releases first new studio album in a decade, 'Caranaval de Luz'
results.content: U2 just released a new album after nine years of no new content. And fans are already rocking out to the new songs. Details on the Irish rock band’s comeback by Ophelie Jacobson.

results.title: Half a million people gather for an open-air mass by Pope Leo in Peru
results.content: Pope Leo said it was a "joy to be back" in his second home of Chiclayo, where he made his name as a bishop. This is the latest stop on his South America tour, the very tour that saw fears of cancellation after the Pope underwent surgery for lung cancer. Story by Vedika Bahl.

results.title: Microsoft's widespread outages caused global chaos, including in the healthcasre industry
results.content: Microsoft says it is seeing improvements in its service availability after an hours-long disruption knocked out its platforms including Outlook and Teams. The outage has affected hundreds of millions of people across the globe. The healthcare industry was among those impacted, as Ophelie Jacobson explains.

results.title: France fend off South African comeback to clinch long-awaited win in Paris
results.content: Twenty-one years after last beating the Springboks in Paris, Les Bleus held out for a 21-19 win over the world champions on Friday after a nailbiting finale. Antoine Dupont and company are now one step away from reaching the Nations Championship final in London.
